Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration this node formalizes. Keep it 1-to-1: one
  blueprint node ↔ one Lean declaration, signatures matching.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. If a Lean helper exists with no math counterpart,
  write its LaTeX statement so the 1-to-1 correspondence holds.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One declaration's worth per node.** Don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/references

`references/` is a **shared library at the workspace root** — one library for
every project — holding the original source material a blueprint is formalised
from (papers, books, notes). It is indexed by `references/manifest.yaml`. Per-
project files live under each project's directory; `references/` does not — it is
always at the workspace root, and `references/**` is writable from any agent.

A blueprint node derived from a source carries a `\source{...}` anchor. Those
anchors are the audit trail from a formal statement back to where it came from,
so they must be **true**, not plausible.

## The one rule: read before you cite

**Never add a `\source{...}` anchor to a source you have not actually read.** Do
not infer a citation from a title, a topic, a theorem number, or your own prior
knowledge of the result. An anchor asserts "this exact statement/proof appears
here" — if you haven't opened the referenced material and confirmed it, you don't
know that, and a wrong anchor is worse than none (it sends the next reader/agent
to the wrong place and launders a guess as provenance).

Concretely, before writing `\source{...}`:
1. Confirm the source exists in `references/manifest.yaml`. If it isn't there,
   get it in first (see below) — don't cite a slug that doesn't resolve.
2. Open the actual content — the TeX, or the transcribed page — and confirm the
   statement/proof you're anchoring is really there.
3. Only then write the anchor.

## Anchor forms — pick by what the source actually is

The manifest's `read` field for each entry tells you which case you're in.

- **The source has LaTeX** (arXiv e-print, an open `.tex`, etc.): read the TeX
  directly and cite the source as a whole — `\source{slug}`. Do **not** invent a
  `page-NNNN`; a TeX source has no rendered pages, so a page number would be
  fabricated. If the manifest documents stable sub-ids for the source (a section
  or label id), you may use `\source{slug:<id>}`, but only an id that exists.
- **The source is PDF-only** (no usable TeX): cite the transcribed page,
  `\source{slug:page-NNNN}`, where `page-NNNN` is a real file under
  `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` that you have read. If that page hasn't
  been transcribed yet, transcribe it first (below) — don't cite a page that
  doesn't exist on disk.

Multiple anchors may be comma-separated: `\source{slug:page-0042, other:page-0007}`.

## Getting a source into the library

Don't fetch and stash sources ad hoc. Spawn the **`reference-retriever`** subagent
(by name, through your engine's native subagent mechanism) with whatever you have
— topic, arXiv ID, DOI, title, URL, target page range. It downloads the original
(preferring TeX, keeping the PDF), verifies the file is real (not a paywall/login
page named `.pdf`), organises it under `references/<slug>/`, and registers it in
`references/manifest.yaml`. Wait for it, then cite from what it wrote.

## Extracting the LaTeX from a PDF-only source

When there is no reliable TeX and you need the actual math (to read it, or to cite
a page), **extract it with the proper tool — don't eyeball the PDF and paraphrase.**
The extraction path is the **`page-transcriber`** subagent, which renders each page
to an image and **vision-transcribes** it into one self-contained
`references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` per page.

- **Vision, never OCR.** OCR mangles math (subscripts, operators, alignment);
  reading the rendered page image with a vision model preserves it. This is a hard
  rule of the transcription flow.
- **A small vision model is usually enough.** Faithful page transcription doesn't
  need a frontier model — a cheap vision-capable model (e.g. Haiku) running in the
  background typically suffices, which is what the config is for:

  ```yaml
  references:
    transcription:
      harness: <optional harness>
      model: <cheap vision-capable model, e.g. a Haiku-class model>
  ```

  Don't pick the model inside the prompt; pin it in config so every transcription
  uses the same cheap vision model. When unset it falls back to the subagent/Ground
  harness.
- **Keep each call ≤5 pages.** Longer ranges lose accuracy; split a big range
  across several `page-transcriber` calls.

## Reading transcriptions correctly

- A transcribed page is `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` where `NNNN` is the
  **PDF page index**, which often differs from the printed page number. The
  manifest entry's `read` field records the `page_offset` and any fallback that
  actually worked — respect it when mapping "Theorem 3.4 on p. 12" to a file.
- Read the whole page file before citing it; a page can hold several results.

## The manifest at a glance

One entry per source (the `reference-retriever` owns the full schema):

```yaml
references:
  - slug: <slug>
    title: <title>
    source: <arXiv ID / DOI / URL>
    status: ok            # or: not_found
    files:
      - { path: <slug>/<slug>.pdf, format: pdf }
      - { path: <slug>/source.tex, format: tex }        # if TeX obtained
      - { path: <slug>/tex/page-0042.tex, format: tex } # if transcribed
    read: "Read TeX when present; else page anchors slug:page-NNNN. page_offset: ..."
```

If a source can't be found and verified, it's recorded `status: not_found` — treat
that as "no citation available," and write no math attributed to it.

Related skills: `blueprint-conventions` for where `\source{...}` sits among the
other blueprint annotations, and `leandag` for how a node's `sources` feed the DAG.

154	/-- The common refinement of two covers: `Spec` of the tensor product of the carriers,
155	i.e. the fiber product of the covering spectra over the base. -/
156	noncomputable def prod (E E' : EtaleCover A) : EtaleCover A :=
157	  haveI : Algebra.Etale A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
158	    Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
159	  haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
160	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
161	  .of (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
162	
163	/-- The carrier of the common refinement is the tensor product of the carriers. -/
164	noncomputable def prodEquiv (E E' : EtaleCover A) :
165	    (E.prod E').Carrier ≃ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier :=
166	  haveI : Algebra.Etale A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
167	    Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
168	  haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
169	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
170	  ofEquiv (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
171	
172	/-- The first refinement map of the common refinement. -/
173	noncomputable def prodInl (E E' : EtaleCover A) : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.prod E').Carrier :=
174	  ((E.prodEquiv E').symm.toAlgHom).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
175	
176	/-- The second refinement map of the common refinement. -/
177	noncomputable def prodInr (E E' : EtaleCover A) : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.prod E').Carrier :=
178	  ((E.prodEquiv E').symm.toAlgHom).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
179	
180	/-- Combine refinement maps out of the two factors into one out of the common
181	refinement (the universal property of the fiber product of the covering spectra). -/
182	noncomputable def prodLift {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
183	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (E.prod E').Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier :=
184	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift f g fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _).comp
185	    (E.prodEquiv E').toAlgHom
186	
187	@[simp]
188	theorem prodLift_comp_prodInl {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
189	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (prodLift f g).comp (E.prodInl E') = f := by
190	  ext x
191	  simp [prodLift, prodInl]
192	
193	@[simp]
194	theorem prodLift_comp_prodInr {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
195	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (prodLift f g).comp (E.prodInr E') = g := by
196	  ext x
197	  simp [prodLift, prodInr]
198	
199	theorem prod_refines_left (E E' : EtaleCover A) : (E.prod E').Refines E :=
200	  ⟨E.prodInl E'⟩
201	
202	theorem prod_refines_right (E E' : EtaleCover A) : (E.prod E').Refines E' :=
203	  ⟨E.prodInr E'⟩
204	
205	/-- Directedness of the refinement preorder: any two covers have a common refinement. -/
206	theorem exists_refines_prod (E E' : EtaleCover A) :
207	    ∃ E'' : EtaleCover A, E''.Refines E ∧ E''.Refines E' :=
208	  ⟨E.prod E', E.prod_refines_left E', E.prod_refines_right E'⟩
209	
210	/-- The trivial cover of `Spec A` by itself. -/
211	noncomputable def self (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : EtaleCover A :=
212	  .of A (by
213	    rw [show algebraMap A A = RingHom.id A from rfl, PrimeSpectrum.comap_id]
214	    exact fun p => ⟨p, rfl⟩)
215	
216	/-- The carrier of the trivial cover is the base ring. -/
217	noncomputable def selfEquiv (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : (self A).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] A :=
218	  ofEquiv A _
219	
220	/-- The canonical refinement map from the trivial cover to any cover (algebra side: the
221	structure map of the carrier, through the trivial carrier's identification with `A`). -/
222	noncomputable def fromSelf (E : EtaleCover A) : (self A).Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier :=
223	  (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).comp (selfEquiv A).toAlgHom
224	
225	/-- Every cover refines the trivial cover: the trivial cover is the base point of the
226	refinement preorder. -/
227	theorem refines_self (E : EtaleCover A) : E.Refines (self A) :=
228	  ⟨E.fromSelf⟩
229	
230	/-! ## Base change -/
231	
232	section baseChange
233	
234	variable (A' : Type u) [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A']
235	
236	/-- The base change of a cover along `A → A'`: the cover of `Spec A'` with carrier
237	`A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier` (the fiber product of the covering spectrum with the new base). -/
238	noncomputable def baseChange (E : EtaleCover A) : EtaleCover A' :=
239	  .of (A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
240	
241	/-- The carrier of the base-changed cover is the base-changed carrier. -/
242	noncomputable def baseChangeEquiv (E : EtaleCover A) :
243	    (E.baseChange A').Carrier ≃ₐ[A'] A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
244	  ofEquiv (A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
245	
246	/-- The canonical map from the carrier of a cover to the carrier of its base change,
247	as a map of `A`-algebras. -/
248	noncomputable def baseChangeInclude (E : EtaleCover A) :
249	    E.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.baseChange A').Carrier :=
250	  (((E.baseChangeEquiv A').symm.toAlgHom).restrictScalars A).comp
251	    Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
252	
253	/-- The base change of a refinement map: `A' ⊗[A] —` on carriers, through the
254	presented-carrier identifications — the functoriality of `baseChange` in the cover. -/
255	noncomputable def baseChangeMap {E F : EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
256	    (E.baseChange A').Carrier →ₐ[A'] (F.baseChange A').Carrier :=
257	  ((F.baseChangeEquiv A').symm.toAlgHom).comp
258	    ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A' A') h).comp (E.baseChangeEquiv A').toAlgHom)
259	
260	/-- Base change of refinement maps commutes with the canonical inclusions into the base
261	change. -/
262	theorem baseChangeMap_comp_baseChangeInclude {E F : EtaleCover A}
263	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
264	    ((baseChangeMap A' h).restrictScalars A).comp (E.baseChangeInclude A')
265	      = (F.baseChangeInclude A').comp h := by
266	  ext x
267	  simp [baseChangeMap, baseChangeInclude]
268	
269	end baseChange

271	/-! ## Covers of a field: single-factor refinement -/
272	
273	section field
274	
275	variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
276	
277	/-- The carrier of a cover of a field (indeed, of any nontrivial base) is nontrivial. -/
278	theorem nontrivial_carrier (E : EtaleCover A) [Nontrivial A] : Nontrivial E.Carrier :=
279	  PrimeSpectrum.nonempty_iff_nontrivial.mp
280	    ⟨(E.comap_surjective (Nonempty.some inferInstance)).choose⟩
281	
282	/-- **Field cofinality**: over a field, every presented étale cover is refined by a finite
283	separable field extension.  This single-factor refinement is what makes field-extension
284	covers cofinal among étale covers of `Spec K`: the étale carrier is a finite product of
285	finite separable extensions of `K`, and projection to any one factor still covers the
286	(one-point) spectrum of `K`. -/
287	theorem exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom (E : EtaleCover K) :
288	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L)
289	      (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L), Nonempty (E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L) := by
290	  haveI : Nontrivial E.Carrier := E.nontrivial_carrier
291	  obtain ⟨I, hI, Ai, hfield, halg, e, h⟩ :=
292	    (Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod K E.Carrier).mp inferInstance
293	  haveI : Nonempty I := by
294	    by_contra hempty
295	    haveI : IsEmpty I := not_nonempty_iff.mp hempty
296	    haveI : Subsingleton E.Carrier := e.toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mpr inferInstance
297	    exact false_of_nontrivial_of_subsingleton E.Carrier
298	  obtain ⟨i⟩ := ‹Nonempty I›
299	  exact ⟨Ai i, hfield i, halg i, (h i).1, (h i).2,
300	    ⟨(Pi.evalAlgHom K Ai i).comp e.toAlgHom⟩⟩
301	
302	variable (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
303	
304	instance : Algebra.Etale K L where
305	  formallyEtale := Algebra.FormallyEtale.of_isSeparable K L
306	  finitePresentation :=
307	    (Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType (R := K) (A := L)).mp inferInstance
308	
309	/-- A finite separable field extension as an étale cover of `Spec K` (the spectrum map
310	between the one-point spectra is trivially surjective). -/
311	noncomputable def ofField : EtaleCover K :=
312	  .of L fun _ => ⟨default, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
313	
314	/-- The carrier of the field cover is the field extension itself. -/
315	noncomputable def ofFieldEquiv : (ofField (K := K) L).Carrier ≃ₐ[K] L :=
316	  ofEquiv L _
317	
318	end field
319	
320	end EtaleCover

322	end Algebra

9	/-!
10	# The relative Picard functor on affine test algebras
11	
12	The étale sheafification of the relative Picard functor is computed over *affine* test
13	objects, where a test object is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra `A` (the landed
14	`AlgebraicGeometry.overSpec k A : Over (Spec k)`) and a test map is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra
15	map.  This file provides the algebra-indexed face of the relative Picard functor:
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.overSpecMap f`: `Spec` of a `k`-algebra map `f : A →ₐ[k] B`, as a
18	  morphism `overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A` of `Over (Spec k)`, strictly functorial
19	  (`overSpecMap_id`, `overSpecMap_comp`).
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap C f`: restriction of relative Picard classes along
21	  `Spec f`, a group homomorphism `relPic C (overSpec k A) →* relPic C (overSpec k B)`,
22	  covariantly functorial in the algebra (`relPicAlgMap_id`, `relPicAlgMap_comp`).
23	
24	The étale plus construction (`Picard/PicEtAff.lean`) consumes only this interface: descent
25	classes on an étale cover are an equalizer of two `relPicAlgMap`s, and all refinement
26	transports are `relPicAlgMap`s of `A`-algebra maps restricted to `k`.
27	-/
28	
29	set_option autoImplicit false
30	
31	universe u
32	
33	open CategoryTheory
34	
35	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
36	
37	section OverSpecMap
38	
39	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
40	variable {A B C' D : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
41	  [CommRing C'] [Algebra k C'] [CommRing D] [Algebra k D]
42	
43	/-- `Spec` of a `k`-algebra map, as a morphism of `Over (Spec k)`. -/
44	noncomputable def Over.overSpecMap (f : A →ₐ[k] B) : overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A :=
45	  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f.toRingHom)) (by
46	    dsimp
47	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, AlgHom.comp_algebraMap])
48	
49	@[simp]
50	lemma Over.overSpecMap_left (f : A →ₐ[k] B) :
51	    (Over.overSpecMap f).left = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f.toRingHom) :=
52	  rfl
53	
54	private lemma spec_map_id_alg :
55	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (AlgHom.id k A).toRingHom) = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) := by
56	  rw [show CommRingCat.ofHom (AlgHom.id k A).toRingHom = 𝟙 (CommRingCat.of A) from rfl,
57	    Spec.map_id]
58	
59	private lemma spec_map_comp_alg (f : A →ₐ[k] B) (g : B →ₐ[k] C') :
60	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (g.comp f).toRingHom)
61	      = (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom g.toRingHom) :
62	            Spec (CommRingCat.of C') ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of B))
63	          ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f.toRingHom) := by
64	  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
65	  rfl
66	
67	@[simp]
68	lemma Over.overSpecMap_id : Over.overSpecMap (AlgHom.id k A) = 𝟙 (overSpec k A) := by
69	  ext : 1
70	  exact spec_map_id_alg
71	
72	@[simp]
73	lemma Over.overSpecMap_comp (f : A →ₐ[k] B) (g : B →ₐ[k] C') :
74	    Over.overSpecMap (g.comp f) = Over.overSpecMap g ≫ Over.overSpecMap f := by
75	  ext : 1
76	  exact spec_map_comp_alg f g
77	
78	end OverSpecMap

80	section RelPicAlgMap
81	
82	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
83	variable {A B C' : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
84	  [CommRing C'] [Algebra k C']
85	
86	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along `Spec` of a `k`-algebra map: the
87	algebra-indexed face of the relative Picard functor, covariant in the algebra. -/
88	noncomputable def relPicAlgMap (f : A →ₐ[k] B) :
89	    relPic C (overSpec k A) →* relPic C (overSpec k B) :=
90	  relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap f)
91	
92	@[simp]
93	lemma relPicAlgMap_id (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
94	    relPicAlgMap C (AlgHom.id k A) x = x := by
95	  rw [relPicAlgMap, Over.overSpecMap_id]
96	  exact relPicMap_id C x
97	
98	lemma relPicAlgMap_comp (f : A →ₐ[k] B) (g : B →ₐ[k] C') (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
99	    relPicAlgMap C (g.comp f) x = relPicAlgMap C g (relPicAlgMap C f x) := by
100	  rw [relPicAlgMap, Over.overSpecMap_comp]
101	  exact relPicMap_comp C (Over.overSpecMap f) (Over.overSpecMap g) x
102	
103	end RelPicAlgMap

9	/-!
10	# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests
11	
12	For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
13	Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
18	refinement.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
23	  `h` of covers.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
25	  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
26	  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
27	  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
28	  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
29	  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
30	  algebra.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
32	  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
33	  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
34	  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
36	  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
37	  descent datum.
38	
39	The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
40	covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
41	under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
42	-/
43	
44	set_option autoImplicit false
45	
46	universe u
47	
48	open CategoryTheory
49	
50	open scoped TensorProduct
51	
52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
53	
54	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
55	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
56	
57	noncomputable section
58	
59	/-! ## Descent classes on an étale cover -/
60	
61	/-- The first coprojection from the carrier of a cover into its self-tensor product over
62	the base — the algebra face of the first projection of the double cover
63	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B) → Spec B` — as a `k`-algebra map. -/
64	def doubleInl (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
65	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
67	
68	/-- The second coprojection into the self-tensor product; see `doubleInl`. -/
69	def doubleInr (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
70	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
71	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight).restrictScalars k
72	
73	/-- The subgroup of relative Picard classes on an étale cover of the test algebra
74	satisfying the descent condition: equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double
75	cover. -/
76	def descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
77	    Subgroup (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
78	  MonoidHom.eqLocus
79	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E))
80	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E))
81	
82	lemma mem_descentClasses_iff {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
83	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} :
84	    x ∈ descentClasses C E ↔
85	      relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
86	        = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x :=
87	  Iff.rfl
88	
89	/-! ## Transport along refinement maps -/
90	
91	private lemma doubleInl_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
92	    (doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
93	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) := by
94	  ext x
95	  simp [doubleInl]
96	
97	private lemma doubleInr_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
98	    (doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
99	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) := by
100	  ext x
101	  simp [doubleInr]
102	
103	/-- The descent condition is natural in the cover: pullback along a refinement map sends
104	descent classes to descent classes. -/
105	lemma relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
106	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)}
107	    (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
108	    relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x ∈ descentClasses C F := by
109	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff] at hx ⊢
110	  calc relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x)
111	      = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x :=
112	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
113	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
114	          (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [doubleInl_comp h]
115	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
116	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) := relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
117	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
118	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by rw [hx]
119	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
120	          (doubleInr E)) x := (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
121	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x := by
122	        rw [doubleInr_comp h]
123	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x) :=
124	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
125	
126	/-- Transport of descent classes along a refinement map of covers. -/
127	def descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
128	    descentClasses C E →* descentClasses C F :=
129	  ((relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k)).comp (descentClasses C E).subtype).codRestrict _
130	    fun x => relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses C h x.2
131	
132	@[simp]
133	lemma descentMap_coe {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
134	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
135	    (descentMap C h x : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
136	      = relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
137	  rfl
138	
139	@[simp]
140	lemma descentMap_id {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (x : descentClasses C E) :
141	    descentMap C (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier) x = x := by
142	  ext
143	  rw [descentMap_coe,
144	    show (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k = AlgHom.id k E.Carrier from rfl]
145	  exact relPicAlgMap_id C _
146	
147	lemma descentMap_comp {E F G : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
148	    (h' : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
149	    descentMap C (h'.comp h) x = descentMap C h' (descentMap C h x) := by
150	  ext
151	  rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe,
152	    show (h'.comp h).restrictScalars k
153	      = (h'.restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) from rfl]

156	/-- **Generalized refinement-map independence**, the keystone of the plus construction:
157	a class satisfying the descent condition restricts equally along any two `A`-algebra maps
158	out of the cover carrier — into an arbitrary test algebra, not merely another cover.  The
159	pair `(j₁, j₂)` factors jointly through the double cover of the source, where the descent
160	condition identifies the two pullbacks. -/
161	theorem relPicAlgMap_congr {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
162	    [Algebra k R] [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower k A R] (j₁ j₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R)
163	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
164	    relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by
165	  set H : E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R :=
166	    Algebra.TensorProduct.lift j₁ j₂ fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _ with hH
167	  have key₁ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) = j₁.restrictScalars k := by
168	    ext y
169	    simp [hH, doubleInl]
170	  have key₂ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) = j₂.restrictScalars k := by
171	    ext y
172	    simp [hH, doubleInr]
173	  calc relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x
174	      = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [key₁]
175	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) :=
176	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
177	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by
178	        have hx' : relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
179	            = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x := hx
180	        rw [hx']
181	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E)) x :=
182	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _).symm
183	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by rw [key₂]

189	    (h₁ h₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
190	    descentMap C h₁ x = descentMap C h₂ x :=
191	  Subtype.ext (relPicAlgMap_congr C h₁ h₂ x.2)

195	/-- Two descent-class representatives are identified when they agree after transport to a
196	common refinement.  By `descentMap_congr` the choice of transport maps is immaterial, so

198	instance picEtAffSetoid : Setoid (Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) where
199	  r p q := ∃ (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : p.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)

202	    constructor
203	    · exact fun p => ⟨p.1, AlgHom.id A _, AlgHom.id A _, rfl⟩
204	    · rintro p q ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩
205	      exact ⟨F, g, f, hfg.symm⟩
206	    · rintro p q r ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ ⟨G, f', g', hfg'⟩
207	      refine ⟨F.prod G, (F.prodInl G).comp f, (F.prodInr G).comp g', ?_⟩
208	      rw [descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hfg, ← descentMap_comp, ← descentMap_comp,
209	        descentMap_congr C ((F.prodInl G).comp g) ((F.prodInr G).comp f') q.2,

8	/-!
9	# Functoriality of the étale plus construction in the test algebra
10	
11	The étale-plus Picard group `PicEtAff C A` is functorial in the affine test: a base
12	extension `A → A'` restricts a plus class by base-changing its representing cover
13	(`Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChange`) and transporting the descent datum along the canonical
14	inclusion of the carrier into its base change.  Following the mathlib idiom for maps along
15	base extensions, the extension is carried as instances `[Algebra A A'] [IsScalarTower k A A']`
16	rather than as an explicit `k`-algebra map.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentBaseChange C A' E`: transport of descent classes along the base
19	  change of the cover — well-posed because the two coprojections of the base-changed double
20	  cover restrict to `A`-algebra maps out of the original carrier, so the keystone
21	  `relPicAlgMap_congr` applies.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map C A'`: the induced restriction homomorphism
23	  `PicEtAff C A →* PicEtAff C A'`.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_unit`: naturality of the unit of the plus construction.
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_id`, `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_map`: the functor
26	  laws — both are instances of `relPicAlgMap_congr`, which erases the difference between
27	  any two transports out of the same descent class.
28	
29	Together with the unit (`PicEtAff.unit`), this is the presheaf structure of the one-step
30	étale plus of the relative Picard functor on affine tests; the comparison theorems
31	(separatedness, rigidification under a section) consume this interface.
32	-/

67	
68	**Semantic pin.** For any scheme `X`, the Picard group *of record* is the Čech cohomology

76	functors and elements defined in this spec. Therefore the comparison

82	### 2.1 Index discipline: pointed covers, arbitrary opens
83	
84	```lean
85	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. -/
86	structure Scheme.PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
87	  opens : X → X.Opens
88	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x

93	Decision rationale (each alternative was weighed):
94	
95	- **Not finite covers, not affine covers, not `Set X.Opens`.** Pointed covers give:
96	  (a) *smallness for free* — the index type is the fixed carrier `X : Type u`, so the sigma type
97	  in §2.3 stays in `Type u`; (b) *canonical refinement maps* — a refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰` refines
98	  **indexwise** (`𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`), so the cocycle-restriction map needs no choice of a
99	  reindexing function and no "independence of the refinement map" lemma at the carrier level;
100	  (c) *directedness by pointwise `⊓`* (`(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x := 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x`), so the
101	  refinement colimit is filtered; (d) *clean pullback* — for `f : X ⟶ Y` the pulled-back cover is

104	  (pullback collapses indices).

106	  pointed cover is refined by a pointed affine cover (`x ↦` an affine open neighbourhood inside
107	  `𝒰.opens x`; the choice lives inside a `Prop`, so no data escapes). This is where the

163	- The relation is an equivalence *because the poset is directed* (common refinement by pointwise

175	### 2.4 Group structure: multiplicative, `CommGrpCat`-valued
176	
177	**Decision: multiplicative.** Justification (each item load-bearing):
178

### 4.4 Why one plus suffices: the separatedness ledger

**(C1) Separatedness** (`Picard/Separatedness.lean`): for affine `T` and a presented étale
cover `E`, the map `relPic C T → relPic C (T' E)` is injective. This is Kleiman 2.5(1)
restricted to what we consume, recast on cocycles. Proof ledger (all pieces named because they
are shared bricks):

1. `sectionsBaseChange` (`Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean`): for `V ⊆ C.left` affine open
   and a `k`-algebra `A`, `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, V_A) ≅ Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] A`, naturally.
   *Shared with*: the T₀ dual-numbers engine (`A = k[ε]`, recon lesson 7) and the χ-ledger over
   field extensions (`A = K`). One brick, three consumers.
2. `universalSections` (`Picard/UniversalSections.lean`): `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, ⊤) = A` for
   every `k`-algebra `A` — the two-cover H⁰ slice: the complex
   `Γ(V₀) ⊕ Γ(V₁) → Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` has `H⁰ = k` (Wave 1), stays exact under the flat `⊗[k] A`
   by 1. This is our discharge of Kleiman's `ex:gc&r` hypothesis in the form actually consumed.
3. `prPullback_injective`: `CechPic.map (snd C T).left` is injective for affine `T` — a unit
   cocycle on `C ⊗ T` trivializing must have come from `T`, because

8	/-!
9	# The relative Picard functor of a curve
10	
11	For a scheme `C` over a field `k` (an object of `Over (Spec k)`) this file defines the
12	relative Picard functor of Grothendieck–Kleiman:
13	$$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T) \;=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \times_k T)\,/\,
14	  \operatorname{Pic}(T),$$
15	line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T` modulo classes pulled back from the test object `T`
16	along the second projection. The quotient — never the absolute `Pic(C ⊗ T)`, which is
17	not even a separated presheaf in any useful sense — is the functor that étale
18	sheafification and the representability theorem consume.
19	
20	Products are the cartesian-monoidal product of `Over (Spec k)` (chosen pullbacks of
21	schemes): `C ⊗ T`, projection `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`, matching the vocabulary
22	of the challenge statement file.
23	
24	## Main declarations
25	
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase C T`: the subgroup of `(C ⊗ T).left.CechPic` of classes
27	  pulled back from `T` along the second projection.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic C T`: the relative Picard group, the quotient by
29	  `picFromBase C T`, a `CommGroup`; `relPicMk` is the projection, with
30	  `relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff` the exact coset relation (a genuine range condition, no
31	  choice, no `Nonempty (≅)`).
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMap C g`: restriction along `g : T' ⟶ T`, descended from
33	  pullback of Čech classes along `C ◁ g`.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicFunctor C`: the relative Picard functor
35	  `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
